# Rules: Apps, extensions and connections

**Covers:** Tool servers (MCP), the Directory, connectors, import, web services, sign-in apps: `mcp/`, `mcpserver/`, `connectors/`, `connections/`, `integrations/`.

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **Packs, spreadsheets and the phone** (v1.291.0, deep review wave 4).
  (io-01) A read_only openpyxl sheet RE-PARSES ITS XML FROM ROW 1 on every
  `iter_rows(min_row=r, max_row=r)`, so a per-row lookup is O(rows²) (1,000
  rows with one blank column: 25 s). `_read_xlsx` walks the value and formula
  passes in LOCKSTEP by POSITION (`enumerate` + `next(frows)`), opening the
  formula pass lazily on the first `None` cell; never `.row`/`.coordinate` —
  an unwritten blank arrives as `EmptyCell`, which has neither (that was a
  crash, not just a slowdown). The pin is a RATIO (blank column vs none).
  (io-02) `MCPClient._request` runs a synchronous transport OFF THE LOOP
  (`asyncio.to_thread`) under a per-transport lock (ids and the single stdout
  reader never interleave); `StdioTransport` reads on a reader thread + queue
  with a deadline; on expiry or cancel `abort()` KILLS the child (a parked
  readline must never keep owning the pipe) so the next call respawns. The
  registry deadline (`config.tool_call_timeout_s`) is the ONE bound on a
  pack call: a registry transport takes `request_timeout=None`; only
  deadline-less callers (the LTM brain, driven through `asyncio.run`) get
  `DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S`. A transport floor shorter than the caller's
  deadline is a bug. (io-05) The child is spawned with `encoding="utf-8",
  errors="replace"` (MCP stdio is UTF-8 by spec; cp1252 raised on C3 8D) and
  `stdio_shim` wraps `sys.stdin/stdout.buffer` in UTF-8 TextIOWrappers.
  (io-06) `_ensure_started` respawns when `_proc.poll()` is not None; EOF /
  OSError / BrokenPipe mark the process dead and raise an `MCPError` that
  NAMES the pack and says it restarts on the next call — never auto-retry
  (a tools/call may have had side effects). `close()` kills the process TREE
  (kill-on-close Job on Windows — npx runs cmd.exe with node as a grandchild —
  then the pipes, so a parked readline returns). (io-03) The phone poll
  never awaits a session: `_handle` creates it, acks inline, and runs it in a
  tracked task (`_spawn_delivery`; set + done-callback; cancelled at
  lifespan shutdown) that sends the summary and `_safe_append`s it; the
  inflight marker covers DISPATCH only. Two restart paths tell the phone: a
  crash → boot reconcile stamps `interrupted_at` → `notify_interrupted(since=
  boot)` (sent to the single allowed sender's chat when the channel has no
  `chat_id`); a graceful shutdown → `cancel_background()` sets
  `_shutting_down` and the cancelled delivery RE-ARMS the inflight marker so
  the next boot's `_recover_inflight` sends `DROPPED_REPLY` — a desktop
  Cancel does not re-arm. A pin that awaits `_handle` then reads the outcome
  needs `await poller.drain()`. (io-04) The frozen exe's entry is the Typer
  CLI, so `-m iron_jarvis.mcpserver.stdio_shim` died with "No such option":
  hidden `ironjarvis mcp-stdio` (lazy import, nothing on stdout but the
  protocol); `CodexRecipe.config_text` writes `["mcp-stdio"]` under
  `sys.frozen`, else `["-m", module]`, and `_shim_available` agrees.
  RELEASE CHECKLIST: after an installer builds, run
  `"<install>\resources\daemon\ironjarvis.exe" mcp-stdio` with
  IRONJARVIS_MCP_URL/TOKEN set and feed one `initialize` line — one JSON-RPC
  line must come back (exit 0). Pins: `tests/test_xlsx_blank_cells_v1291.py`,
  `test_mcp_stdio_transport_v1291.py` (+ `tests/fixtures/stdio_mcp_server_v1291.py`),
  `test_phone_job_background_v1291.py`, `test_codex_frozen_shim_v1291.py`.

- **A pack SAYS WHY it failed, where the model and the user each read**
  (v1.342.0, "the pack says why", the first wave of the reliability/self-
  repair arc the user approved 2026-10-16; six doer/reviewer lanes + an
  integrator, every lane approved round 1 against the real diff with
  mutations). STDERR (`mcp/client.py`): a stdio pack is spawned with
  `stderr=PIPE` drained on its own daemon thread into a bounded ring
  (`STDERR_RING_LINES` 40 / 8 KB / 1000-char lines) that OUTLIVES `close()`;
  `StdioTransport.stderr_tail()` / `MCPClient.stderr_tail()` answer the ring
  masked (`detections.redact.mask`, BEFORE the cuts) and cut to
  `STDERR_TAIL_MAX` (2000), "" for HTTP/fake/faulting transports; the EOF and
  broken-pipe `MCPServerStopped` texts keep their old words byte-identical
  then add "; its last output: <≤ 600 chars, newlines → ' | '>" and
  `SETTINGS_FIX_SENTENCE` ("If it needs a key or setting, the user can fix
  it in Settings → Tools."); close() joins the reader ≤ 0.5 s, never blocks.
  STATUS (`mcp/tools.py`): `_connect_with_timeout` raises `PackLoadFailed
  (cause, stderr_tail)`; `_load_one_server`/`mcp_tools(errors=)` hand the
  failure back EVEN WHEN `record=False` (`errors[name] = {error, reason,
  fix, stderr_tail}`) — the Test route, the Directory test and the add route
  read it, so a probe reports the REAL error ("advertised no tools" only
  when it really connected and listed none); `classify_load_failure` checks
  the CRASH shape ("closed the connection"/"exit code"/"stopped") BEFORE the
  "connect" branch that misread it as unreachable; the load record carries
  `state` ok|failed|failing|starting (was "ready" — `system_map.py` reads
  "ok"), `failures`, `stderr_tail`; `note_call_failure(name, error)` /
  `note_call_success(name)` are called from `MCPRemoteTool.execute` and
  publish ONE `mcp.pack_failed {name, error, reason, fix}` per episode
  (first failure after a success/reload/load; `set_event_bus` is wired in
  `build_platform` right after `EventBus()`). SECRETS (`mcp/secrets.py`):
  `SECRET_KEY_RX = (?i)(token|key|secret|passw|auth|credential)` on the env
  KEY; `split_env` → plain env + vault values under `vault_name(server,
  key)` = `mcp.<server>.<KEY>`, the stored record keeps `env_secrets[KEY]`
  (the existing spawn-time resolver); POST /mcp/servers refuses the add when
  the vault refuses; GET rows carry `env_keys` + `secret_keys` and NEVER a
  value (an HTTP pack's `auth.value` → `value_set: true`); DELETE removes
  the vault rows AND `<home>/mcp/manifests/<name>.json` (a re-add is a
  first load again); `migrate_mcp_env_secrets(config=, secrets=)` runs in
  `build_platform` BEFORE `_mcp_configs` — idempotent, NAMES logged, a
  refused vault write leaves that entry untouched. CLOSES: `mcp.tools.
  close_tools_clients(tools)` + `unload_pack_tools(registry, name)` are the
  ONE closer (lifted from platform.py, which now delegates); connectors
  disconnect/reconnect and settings `load_app`/`apply_app` close what they
  unregister (the v1.328.1 leak at three more doors). CHAT (lock-step): a
  FAILED `mcp__*` call's `result.error` goes through `_fence_tool_output`
  (fence + injection scan + taint) in BOTH lanes; non-MCP failures keep the
  registry's own words; `ran` stays False. DASHBOARD: ToolsPage `packState()`
  words (Starting / N tools / Didn't start / Failing: N calls), the folded
  "Last output", Retry for failed/failing/zero-tool packs, no green Enabled
  for a broken pack, env by key name, Delete says "Removed."; DirectoryPage
  renders `status: failed` + reason/fix/stderr_tail (`connectors/service.
  _mcp_status` reads the load record for a zero-tool pack); the bell maps
  `mcp.pack_failed` → `/tools` (`BELL_EVENT_TYPES` + `toActivity`). Pins:
  `tests/test_{mcp_stderr_tail,mcp_honest_test,mcp_secrets_vault,
  mcp_close_on_disconnect,chat_mcp_error_fence,integration_pins}_v1342.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/{tools-pack-rows,bell-pack-failed}-v1342.test.tsx`.
  Known: the error's tail folds newlines to ' | ' while `stderr_tail()`
  keeps them. (The Directory `no_tools` detail no longer says "restart":
  v1.351.0 G08 reworded it with `test_wiki_access_v1172`, moved together.)

- **A pack is added through ONE door, from any dialect, and a secret never
  crosses the browser** (v1.343.0, "add a pack in one paste", wave 2 of the
  reliability arc; five lanes + an integrator, K-ui took two review rounds).
  `mcp/import_config.py`: `PackSpec` (dataclass; `to_config()` = the stored/
  launched dict, a stdio spec byte-identical to the v1.342.0 shape;
  `from_config` drops vault names; `preview_row()` never carries a value),
  `safe_name(raw)` (lowercase, non-[a-zA-Z0-9_-] → "-", runs collapsed,
  leading non-letters stripped, ≤ 40, no trailing "-"; the dashboard's
  `lib/mcpImport.safeName` is its TS twin, cross-checked under node on a
  12-name table), `guess_launcher(pkg)` (uvx for pip:/pypi:, underscore
  names and mcp-server-*; npx otherwise), `parse_any(text)` (Claude
  Desktop/Code `mcpServers` incl. per-project, VS Code `mcp.servers`, Codex
  `[mcp_servers.<name>]` TOML, a single server object, a command line, a
  URL (/sse → sse), an `npx mcp-remote <url> --header` line → http; Iron
  Jarvis's own server entries dropped; never raises) and `parse_file`.
  `mcp/import_sources.py`: `scan(platform)` reads ~/.claude.json
  (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), ~/.claude/settings.json, the active project's
  .mcp.json, Claude Desktop, Codex (CODEX_HOME), Cursor, VS Code settings
  (comments + trailing commas via jsonish) READ-ONLY, names only; keys
  `claude-code`/`claude-code-settings`/`claude-code-project`/`claude-desktop`
  /`codex`/`cursor`/`vscode`. ROUTES (`routes/agents.py`): the POST body is
  lifted into module-level `add_mcp_pack(d, body)` and DELETE into
  `remove_mcp_pack` — the ONE add/remove path that `POST /mcp/servers`,
  `POST /mcp/import/apply {text | source, names, overrides, replace}` and
  the npm door all end in; `POST /mcp/import/preview {text}` and
  `GET /mcp/import/sources` answer rows with `env_keys/secret_keys/
  header_names/auth_set/exists/runtime_ready` (the catalog's `launcher_ready`
  resolver) and NEVER a value (a sweep plants 8 sentinels through every door
  and asserts none reaches an answer, config.toml or the log); apply from a
  source re-reads the FILE server-side by its scan key (a path is a 404).
  `McpServerBody` gains transport/url/headers/auth/launcher (a stdio body
  with no command is now a 422 sentence, not the route's old 400); an http
  pack's auth value → vault `mcp.<name>.auth.value` (`auth.secret`), a
  secret-NAMED header → `mcp.<name>.header.<H>` (`header_secrets`, resolved
  in `_build_transport` beside `env_secrets`); GET rows carry `transport`,
  `header_names`, `auth_set` on every row. `PATCH /mcp/servers/{name}` is
  PARTIAL (command, args, env MERGE with secret-named values vaulted, cwd,
  transport, url, headers, auth — `null` clears via `model_fields_set`,
  omitted keeps —, clear_secrets, clear_headers; "" is a value; a rename is
  422; validated like a POST; every vault write before the row persists;
  then `unload_pack_tools` + reload; answer = GET row + `reloaded`/`note`;
  a bare `{auto_approve}` keeps the v1.103.0 answer byte for byte).
  DASHBOARD: `components/tools/AddPack.tsx` (paste / import / HTTP doors →
  one preview list with StatusChip + "already added" + inputs for missing
  secrets), `EditPack.tsx` (prefilled from names only; sends ONLY changed
  fields), `lib/mcpImport.ts`. LIVE-DRIVEN by the integrator: a pasted
  README block launched the real `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`
  (14 tools) with the token vault-only. Pins: `tests/test_mcp_{http_door,
  import_paste,import_sources,edit_pack}_v1343.py`, `tests/
  test_integration_pins_v1343.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/tools-{add,edit}-
  pack-v1343.test.tsx`. Known: (v1.351.0 G12 closed the old args leak: an
  `mcp-remote` `--header` secret, a `--api-key` value or a connection
  string's password in `args` / a url is now vaulted as `arg_secrets` /
  `url_secret` and shown masked — see the v1.351.0 bullet) a PATCH that
  sends `env` to an http pack (or `headers` to a stdio one) writes then
  drops it silently rather than 422ing.

- **Microsoft 365 is LOCKED DOWN for client data: read and draft only, one
  account, the firm's own app, a locked install, the user's own models only**
  (v1.428.0; the user, a CPA firm: "highly secure", the main mailbox, drafts
  only, "local only, always"). THE CARD (`connectors/catalog` `microsoft_365`,
  `locked="ms365"`, `local_only=True`, `command="node"`, `args=[]`,
  `replaces=[MS365_PACKAGE]`): fields = the account-kind choice
  (common/consumers), `MS365_MCP_EXPECTED_USERNAME` (required) and
  `MS365_MCP_CLIENT_ID` (a GUID; REQUIRED for a work account — `NEED_APP`; a
  personal account gets the package's own `DEFAULT_APP`, named explicitly).
  `connectors/ms365.env_for(values, signin_dir)` is THE
  rule: `ENABLED_TOOLS` = `SAFE_TOOLS` (15: calendar/contacts/OneDrive read,
  mail read + `create-draft-email`; never send-mail or calendar writes — the
  package then asks Microsoft for Calendars.Read, Contacts.Read, Files.Read,
  Mail.ReadWrite, measured with its `--list-permissions`),
  `MS365_MCP_CLOUD_TYPE=global`, the email lowercased (the package refuses and
  deletes any other account's sign-in, `rejectUnexpectedLoginAccount`), a work
  account's `MS365_MCP_TENANT_ID` = the email's domain (a single-tenant app
  refuses "common"), and `MS365_MCP_TOKEN_CACHE_PATH` /
  `MS365_MCP_SELECTED_ACCOUNT_PATH` inside `locked_pack.signin_dir`
  (`<install root>/_signin/ms365`; the package encrypts the cache with a key it
  keeps in Windows Credential Manager) — never its shared `%APPDATA%` folder.
  The pack door keeps a LOCKED row's settings PLAIN (`TOKEN_CACHE_PATH` names a
  file, not a secret; the generic split would vault it). THE INSTALL
  (`connectors/locked_pack.py`, `LockedPackage` `MS365` 0.170.2): the lock
  `connectors/locked/ms365/package.json` + `package-lock.json` (188 packages
  without optional ones, every one sha512; keytar a DIRECT dependency so
  `--omit=optional` keeps it and drops the Azure Key Vault extras) installs
  ONCE into `<userData>/mcp-packages/ms365-<lock hash>` (else
  `<home>/mcp-packages`, skipped by `create_backup`) with `npm ci
  --omit=optional --omit=dev --ignore-scripts`, then `npm rebuild keytar`
  ALONE (its prebuilt binary keeps the sign-in key in Windows Credential
  Manager) and its native file checked against a pinned sha256
  (`LockedPackage.native_files`, win32-x64; an unlisted platform skips the
  rebuild), the package's own version checked, a marker written, a failure
  leaving nothing; NO_NODE when Node.js is missing. A changed lock is a new
  folder; nothing updates in place. The pack runs `node <entry>` with the
  install folder as cwd (the package reads a `.env` from its cwd —
  `dist/load-env.js`). THE ROW (`connectors/service.locked_body`, the ONLY
  door: `pack_body` and the chat's `app_connect` refuse a locked card,
  `LOCKED_ELSEWHERE`): command "node", args [entry], cwd, env, `local_only:
  true`, `locked: "ms365"` (`McpServerBody.local_only/locked`, written by
  `mcp/pack_door.add_pack`); `update_mcp_pack` refuses any settings edit of a
  `locked` row (409 `LOCKED_EDIT`; the switch and auto-approve stay). SIGN IN:
  ONE job `microsoft-365-signin` (`ai_clis.SETUP_LAUNCHES`,
  `catalog.signin_launches` — a locked card has no per-choice job);
  `routes/terminals.launch_pane` types the SAVED row's own argv
  (`service.locked_signin`: `resolve_launcher`'s node, the entry, `--login`)
  with the saved env and cwd, or 409s when the row is not exactly what the card
  writes (`_locked_signin_row` round-trips `env_for(answers_from_env(env))`).
  LOCAL ONLY: `mcp/tools` marks a `local_only` row's tools; `execute` refuses
  (`LOCAL_ONLY_APP_REFUSAL`) unless `egress.current_scope()` is on with NO
  `allowed_once`, and a successful call HOLDS the chat:
  `egress.hold_local_only(engine, thread_id, app)` writes `local_only: true` +
  `local_only_holds` (never `updated_at`), or — a new chat's first turn —
  `note_pending_hold(turn_id)` that `POST /chat/turns/{id}/thread` applies.
  `setup_says_local_only` reads holds too; `routes/chat._clean_setup` keeps
  them and forces local_only; the thread PUT merges the STORED holds into
  whatever the page sends (it cannot clear them). The chat page reads them
  (`lib/localOnly.localOnlyHolds`, the chip `data-held`, its title
  `localOnlyHeldTitle`; a press never turns it off; turning it off re-reads the
  chat once). The Handbook section "Microsoft 365, locked down for client
  data" holds the admin-center steps (single-tenant app, public client flows,
  the four Graph permissions + openid/profile/offline_access, admin consent,
  assignment required). OPEN: an existing open (npx) Microsoft 365 row is not
  migrated (it must be disconnected and reconnected); Disconnect does not run
  the package's `--logout` (revoke in Entra); pending holds live in memory (a
  restart between a new chat's first turn and its link loses that hold — the
  tools still refuse outside Local only). REVIEW (each red first, 16
  mutations red): (b) `locked_pack.clean_env` drops every `MS365_MCP_*`,
  ENABLED_TOOLS, READ_ONLY, NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH from the daemon's own
  environment before a locked pack starts (`mcp/tools._build_transport`) and
  before its Sign in terminal starts (`routes/terminals._job_base`) — a stray
  `MS365_MCP_OAUTH_TOKEN` skips the account lock, `MS365_MCP_AUTH_CACHE_COMMAND`
  runs a program with the sign-in; (c) `mcp/tools.chat_only_refusal`: its tools
  answer only when `ctx.session_id == "chat"` and
  `failure_words.current_surface()` is the chat's (never an agent run, a Build
  session or the phone — each carries the answer further); (d)
  `LOCKED_HIDDEN_TOOLS` (logout, remove-account, select-account) are never
  registered; (e) `pack_grants_auto` is False for a `locked` row and PATCH
  `{auto_approve: true}` on one is 409 `LOCKED_ASKS` (both the update path and
  the auto-approve-only fast path); (f) `chat_turn.local_only_scope_for` drops
  `allow_cloud_once` when the saved chat has holds (`egress.thread_holds`), and
  the page offers no "Send once" on a held chat (`CloudAsk.held`,
  `cloudHeldBody`, `dockAskKeyHint`, the refusal's button); (g)
  `egress.note_pending_hold` answers the chat a turn is ALREADY linked to
  (`_TURN_THREADS`, filled by `link_turn_holds` in the link route; one
  `_HOLD_LOCK` for both maps), so a link that lands before the tool reads the
  mail still holds the chat; (h) `locked_pack.unlocked_copy` (name
  `microsoft_365`, or a command line naming `ms-365-mcp-server`, on a row that
  is not `locked`) is refused at `pack_door.add_pack` (409, paste/import/npm
  doors) and never started by `_load_one_server` (its load record says to
  connect from the card); (i) `cap_prior_tool_results(entries, platform)`
  leaves `local_only` tools' rows behind on an escalation (both lanes); (j)
  `POST /chat/threads/{id}/remember` on a local-only or held chat refuses a
  memory base `egress.ltm_connector_is_local` does not call local (409). Pins:
  `tests/test_ms365_locked_v14280.py`, `tests/test_ms365_review_v14280.py`, the
  sign-in-terminal case in `tests/test_microsoft_365_v13560.py`, the v1.428.0
  blocks of `dashboard/__tests__/local-only-chat-v1332.test.tsx`; moved on
  purpose: the v13560/v13580 Microsoft 365 suites (a firm app ID, 18 tools,
  the domain as tenant, the sign-in folder) and both their recorded fixtures.
  STILL OPEN: an agent run under Local only can still use internet tools (a
  general gap, older); the keytar binary was compared with GitHub by size
  only (its sha256 is now pinned on this PC's build).

- **A catalog pack that STARTS today: an unpinned uvx/npx package can break
  when an upstream library moves** (v1.460.0, a USER BUG on the office PC:
  Box connected, never started — `ImportError: cannot import name
  'box_claude_ai_agent_ask' from 'box_ai_agents_toolkit'`). `mcp-server-box`
  0.1.2 (2025-06-05) is Box's last PyPI release (repo discontinued for Box's
  admin-set-up hosted server, which needs an OAuth client flow our remote
  door lacks) and names its libraries unbounded. `connectors/catalog.BOX_ARGS`
  = `uvx --python 3.13 --exclude-newer 2025-06-06 --with boxsdk==3.14.0
  mcp-server-box==0.1.2`, each piece measured: `--exclude-newer` freezes
  every library at release day (pinning one library at a time was
  whack-a-mole: mcp 2.x, pydantic), `boxsdk` is imported but never declared,
  3.13+ is required and June-2025 pydantic-core has no 3.14 build. 30 tools
  answer. `mcp/package_fixes.REPLACED_LAUNCH_LINES` repairs a row at boot only
  when its command AND whole args are exactly what the app wrote (stdio;
  secrets and name kept). `mcp/launch_args.package_arg` reads a line's package
  past launcher option values (`_server_identity`, `_first_package`; `-p` is
  left out: uvx `--python` vs npx `--package`). `classify_load_failure` reads
  a Python ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError or a Node ESM import failure in
  the child's tail (cut at the transport's "; it will be restarted", this
  PC's path removed) as "its package is broken upstream … A missing key or
  setting does not cause this" — checked after the registry 404, before the
  crash branch. A pinned line starts through uvx each time (direct launch
  needs the spec first). Pins: `tests/test_box_pack_v1460.py` (13 mutations
  red; `IJ_LIVE_BOX=1` really starts it). When adding a uvx/npx catalog pack,
  start it from a scratch `UV_CACHE_DIR` first; consider `--exclude-newer`.

- **A catalog names a package that EXISTS; a proxy's picker offers its real

  `@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequentialthinking` — npm never had it (the

  `@modelcontextprotocol/*` name they share. `mcp/package_fixes.
  RENAMED_PACKAGES` (wrong names THE APP shipped, never a guess about a
  user's pack) is applied by `repair_known_package_names` in `build_platform`
  right after `migrate_mcp_env_secrets` (exact arg or `@version` suffix,
  persisted, idempotent). `classify_load_failure` reads an npm / uv registry
  404 FIRST (`_missing_package_in`) as "the package X is not in its
  registry, so the pack's name for it is wrong" — before the crash branch,
  whose "read its last output" sent the user to an npm dump. When adding to
  either catalog: `npm view <pkg>` / PyPI first. NOTE: both catalogs still
  name `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`, which npm marks deprecated
  (still installs; GitHub's own server is a different transport — a
  separate decision). (2) A fleet endpoint's picker rows go through
  `fleet/picker.picker_rows`: a LiteLLM proxy's `/v1/models` answers every
  ALIAS (the user's RTX6000ada: 7 names → 2 servers, two names it no longer
  runs, three embedding names); rows are ONE per deployment (routed model +
  api_base, from the sampler's topology children), keeping the node's
  default name, else the deployment's own id, else the first listed; the
  other names ride `aliases` (templates.analyze_requirements accepts them,
  so a pinned old name is not "not connected"); embedding/reranker names
  (`looks_like_embedding`) are dropped — NEVER the node's default; an empty
  result offers the default; names the children do not route are kept as
  listed (no topology yet / not a proxy). The composer's per-provider model
  panel is `components/chat/FitPanel` (`fitPlacement`: up, capped to the
  room above; down from the row's top when a high row has more room below;
  scrolls) — it ran off the window's top. Pins:
  `tests/test_pack_name_and_endpoint_picker_v13501.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/fit-panel-v13501.test.tsx` (10 mutations, all red).
  v1.350.2 (a REAL bug the v1.350.1 Release gate found, 48-min runner):
  `remove_mcp_pack` unregistered and closed a LOADED pack but never dropped
  its load record (`_LOAD_STATUS`), so a removed pack kept reading "ok" —
  `test_a_pack_deleted_while_starting...` lost its 3 s window (the load
  landed before the DELETE) and failed only on `record is None`. One door
  now: `mcp.tools.forget_load_record(name)`, called by the delete route AND
  `platform._forget_load`. Pinned deterministically in
  `test_deleting_a_pack_that_already_loaded_closes_its_client` (the
  mutation reproduces CI's exact error on an idle machine). Leave GATE_S at
  3 s: another test there depends on the gate EXPIRING.

- **A pack can ASK only where someone can answer, and a pack's model
  request is answered by THE TURN'S model or refused** (v1.324.0, wave C of
  the assistant-ui/tambo borrow list — ideas only). `mcp/interact.py`:
  `InteractionScope` in the ContextVar `MCP_SCOPE`, set by the stream lane
  (`with interaction_scope(_ti.scope_for(tc.id))` INSIDE `_invoke(i)` — never
  held across a generator `yield`) and READ ON THE TRANSPORT WORKER THREAD
  (`asyncio.to_thread` copies the context). `serve_server_request` answers
  ping, bridges `elicitation/create` / `sampling/createMessage` to the loop
  (`run_coroutine_threadsafe`, 0.25 s slices, gives up on the stdio cancel
  token or a stopped loop), declines / -1s with no scope, -32601s the rest;
  `handle_notification` turns the scope's OWN progress token into frames (4/s).
  Initialize declares `{elicitation: {}, sampling: {}}`; `tools/call` carries
  `_meta.progressToken` only under a scope. A scope exists ONLY when the body
  says `mcp_cards: true` (the chat page): a Build pane, the browser sidebar,
  POST /chat, agents, schedules get an instant decline — a card nobody draws
  would park the tool until Stop. `daemon/mcp_turn.TurnInteractions`: side
  queue → `_run_tool_round(side=)` (`_with_side`, drained before `ready`) →
  SSE `mcp_elicitation` / `mcp_sampling` / `mcp_progress` / `mcp_resolved`;
  asks wait with NO clock (answer, Stop, disconnect, turn end); routes
  `/chat/mcp/elicitations|sampling/{id}`, `/mcp/prompts[/get]`,
  `/mcp/resources` (`routes/mcp_interact.py`, 60 s per-pack cache keyed on the
  client). SAMPLING calls `router.complete(provider, model, pin=True)` — the
  new per-call strict pin (both `complete` and `stream`), because without it
  an explicit cloud pick could fail over and send the pack's text to a
  provider the user never chose; low trust / mock / no text / Deny → -1, and
  an answer from another provider is still refused as a backstop. Resources
  (`ChatBody.resources`, ≤ 8) are read at the ATTACHMENTS seam in BOTH lanes
  (`read_turn_resources`, promptguard-scanned, ≤ 20,000 chars) and both carry
  `resources` on the done frame / POST response ALWAYS; the page derives the
  turn's resources from the LAST USER MESSAGE (`appResources`) so Regenerate
  re-reads them. `mcp.tools.live_client(s)` / `forget_live_client` keep a
  client per pack (zero-tool packs too); delete and `_forget_load` forget it.
  Pins: `tests/test_mcp_two_way_v1324.py` (+ `fixtures/mcp_two_way_server_v1324.py`),
  `tests/test_mcp_chat_lane_v1324.py`, `tests/test_mcp_interact_routes_v1324.py`,
  `tests/test_router_call_pin_v1324.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/{mcp-two-way,mcp-page}-v1324.test.tsx`. Known limits:
  url-mode elicitation is declined; a stdio pack waiting on the user holds its
  transport lock (its "/" list waits); sampling `maxTokens` is shown, not
  enforced (the router has no cap); an HTTP pack's wait has no cancel token.

- **An `npx -y` / `uvx` pack's server starts DIRECTLY once its launcher has
  SAID which files it runs; anything uncertain starts exactly as before**
  (v1.415.0; measured on the user's PC: each `npx -y` pack ran cmd.exe ->
  cmd.exe -> `node npx-cli.js` (~81 MB private, idle forever) -> the server,
  and `uvx mcp-server-fetch` ran uvx -> `uv.exe` (~158 MB, idle forever) ->
  trampoline -> python: ~430 MB of launchers for 4 packs).
  `mcp/direct_launch.py`: `parse(resolved_launcher, args, cwd=, env=)` ->
  `LaunchSpec` ONLY for `npx` with `-y`/`--yes` and nothing else before a
  registry spec (`name`, `@latest`, `x.y.z`, `^x.y.z`, `~x.y.z`), `uvx <spec>`
  / `uv tool run <spec>` with no option before the spec, and Windows only;
  `_build_transport` passes it as `StdioTransport(direct=)` (a test double of
  `StdioTransport` must take `**kw`). THE LAUNCHER IS ASKED, never imitated:
  `npx -y --package=<spec> -- node -e …` prints node's path, PATH, and npm's
  `npm_config_cache`/`global_prefix`/`local_prefix`; `uvx --from <spec>
  python -c …` prints `sys.prefix` (measured: the same uv environment `uvx
  <spec>` runs), PATH and `UV`. The answer is kept in
  `<home>/mcp/direct-launch.json` (paths only; the key HASHES launcher, spec,
  cwd and the resolution-relevant env — never the raw env) by ONE background
  worker (`note_started`, after a SUCCESSFUL start, only with a state home —
  `build_platform` calls `set_state_dir(config.home)`; a CLI one-shot or a
  unit test never asks) through `core/procs.run` (120 s bound). `plan(spec)`
  rechecks the disk at EVERY spawn (file reads only): npx's install dir =
  `<cache>/_npx/<sha512(spec)[:16]>` (npm's own hash, pinned against the
  user's real folders), its package.json naming only that package, the
  version satisfying the spec, npm's `getBinFromManifest` choice, a `.js/
  .mjs/.cjs` target inside the package, npm's `.bin/<bin>.cmd` shim in its
  plain `node` form pointing at that file with no extra args, no `.bin/
  node.exe`, NO global copy (`<gp>/node_modules/<name>`) and NO copy npx
  would take from the working folder's project (`_local_copy`: its
  node_modules, `.bin`, own package.json, or any depth via `.package-lock.
  json`; node_modules without that list = unsure); uv: `pyvenv.cfg`,
  `Scripts/<name>.exe`, exactly one dist-info (= the pinned version), not
  also a uv tool elsewhere. `Why.stale` (the answer no longer matches the
  disk) re-asks after the start; a global/local copy or a hold does not.
  FRESHNESS (measured): `npx -y <name>` revalidates against the registry on
  EVERY start (`GET … (cache revalidated)`, 3.9-5.2 s) and `uvx` re-resolves
  every start; a direct start skips that, so a fresh spec (no version /
  `latest`, every uv spec) is refreshed at most once per `REFRESH_S` (a day),
  in the background, and the new version runs from the NEXT start (an npx
  pack's refresh is the READ-ONLY check, see REVIEW 2 (1)). THE START
  (`client.StdioTransport._ensure_started`): Job, suspended start, stderr
  ring, tree kill, UTF-8 pipes all unchanged; the direct handshake is bounded
  by `DIRECT_INIT_TIMEOUT_S` (10 s, via `_read_cap` — `_read`/`_rpc` keep
  their signatures because tests spy them); EOF / no answer / a spawn
  OSError -> `_direct_fell_back`: kill, `_direct_failed` for this transport,
  `note_direct_failed` (no direct start for `FAILED_HOLD_S`, a day, unless
  the launcher later answers with OTHER files), and the launcher started
  ONCE in the same start, said in `launch_info`. A cancel or `shutdown()`
  (new: the connect timeout and `MCPClient.close` call it; a new request
  clears it) during the direct handshake re-raises and starts nothing else —
  and the post-spawn check now also kills a server spawned after a
  shutdown (an old orphan race). The load record (and GET `/mcp/servers`
  rows) gain `launch {direct, how, note}` for npx/uvx packs ONLY (other
  packs byte-identical). Known differences: the server's env lacks npm's
  `npm_*` script variables (PATH gets the same prepended folders, read off
  the ask); the ask right after a launcher start runs npx again beside the
  server that start launched (as a second npx start always could).
  `IRONJARVIS_MCP_DIRECT=off` turns it all off. Pins:
  `tests/test_mcp_direct_launch_v14150.py` (fake npx + uv caches; a REAL
  direct start of `tests/fixtures/direct_launch_v14150/server.js` whose tree
  is `node.exe` alone; ask-then-direct through a stand-in `npx.cmd`; fallback
  on exit and on hang; shutdown mid-handshake), 20 mutations, all red; moved
  on purpose: the `StdioTransport` doubles in `test_mcp_launcher_v1233`,
  `test_connections_honest_v13580`, `test_microsoft_365_v13560`.
  REVIEW (each red first, `tests/test_mcp_direct_launch_review_v14150.py`, 8
  mutations red): (1) npm's `npx.cmd` runs through cmd.exe, which EXPANDS
  `%NAME%` and STRIPS `^` before npx sees the line (measured), so a direct
  start handed the server different args and still answered; `parse` returns
  None for a `.cmd`/`.bat` line carrying any of `% ^ ! " & | < > CR LF`
  (`_CMD_SPECIAL`; an `.exe` launcher has no cmd layer and keeps them). (2) a
  cache behind a junction/subst read as stale (target resolved, package folder
  not) and re-asked npx after EVERY start: both sides resolved now. (3) `uvx
  pkg@1.2` (uv: `==1.2`, met by `1.2.0`) was stale forever: PEP 440 equality
  (`_uv_same_version`). (4) the 10 s cap killed a slow-but-healthy direct
  start and the launcher restart could no longer fit the 15 s connect probe
  (a pack that loaded before failed): the probe sets `transport.start_budget`,
  so the FIRST direct handshake gets the probe's whole bound; if it runs out
  still silent, `give_up_direct_start` holds the pack and `_connect_with_
  timeout` retries the load ONCE through the launcher with a fresh bound
  (worst case 2x the bound at boot). A respawn inside a call (no caller bound)
  keeps the cap. (5) `build_platform` armed background asks in every process,
  CLI one-shots too (an npm/uv install killed half way on exit): `set_state_
  dir(home, ask=defer_mcp)` — every process READS answers, only the daemon
  asks. REVIEW 2 (`tests/test_mcp_direct_launch_refresh_v14150.py`, 15
  mutations red): (1) the daily refresh of an npx pack ran npx, which
  UPGRADES `_npx/<hash>` IN PLACE under a direct server running from it all
  day (npx itself only upgrades at a start). It is now a READ-ONLY check
  (`check`, job "check" from `_job_for`): `npm pack --dry-run --json
  --prefer-online <spec>` with the npm BESIDE the pack's npx (`npx.CMD` ->
  `npm.CMD`), the pack's env and cwd, through `core/procs`, 60 s, on the
  background worker — never `npm view`: MEASURED, `npm view` said 2.1.0 for
  server-everything whose 2.x needs node >= 24, while npx and `npm pack` both
  pick 1.0.0 on node 20 (the same engine-aware `pacote.manifest`); a project
  `.npmrc` registry stopped `npm pack` and npx the same way; `_npx`
  byte-for-byte unchanged (snapshot) and no tarball written. Same version ->
  `asked_at` refreshed; a different one -> `rec["outdated"]`, so `plan` says
  `Why.stale` "version X is out": the NEXT start goes through npx (which
  upgrades at start time, as always) and the ask after that start keeps the
  new answer; an answer whose installed version changed during the check is
  left alone; a check that cannot run or answer changes nothing and is
  retried after `CHECK_RETRY_S` (1 h, in memory). uv is still ASKED daily:
  MEASURED, a new resolution is a NEW `archive-v0` environment, and
  `--refresh`/`--upgrade` left the running environment unchanged (file
  size+mtime snapshot). (2) `direct-launch.json` is written through a temp
  name of its OWN per write (`<name>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp`) + `os.replace`,
  retried while Windows says the file is busy (`_REPLACE_TRIES`), the temp
  removed on failure; two processes x 150 writes each: no torn file and
  no write lost to another writer's temp (the fixed `.tmp` lost 7-12 per
  process to FileNotFoundError, measured); on a loaded PC Windows can still
  refuse a busy replace past the retries (PermissionError, at most a few,
  the pin allows 3). Last writer still wins; a lost answer only means a
  launcher start and a new ask. OPEN: daemon exit
  mid-ask kills an npm install half way; the check downloads the package's
  tarball into npm's own cache (not `_npx`); the daily check can only run at
  a pack start (a pack running for days is checked at its next start).

- **A stray request never ends a sign-in, and an expired sign-in is refused** (v1.499.3 review). The OAuth loopback stops only for a request whose state is a pending one (`UnknownOAuthState` keeps it listening); `complete_oauth` refuses a state older than `_OAUTH_PENDING_TTL` in words. The CLI version probe runs through `core.procs` (bounded, tree-killed). Pins: `tests/test_review_fixes_agents_v1499_3.py`.

- **A call through the tools door is checked again after its card, and has the per-call time limit** (v1.520.0, third review MC5).
  `mcpserver/server._door_refusal` is the one check (the door's session is
  live, the grant still serves a capability, the tool is still permitted);
  `dispatch` runs it on arrival and `_call_tool` runs it again after an
  approved card against `_grant_now` (the pane's or Code session's grant
  re-read from its token store, off the loop). A refusal after Allow goes
  through `invoke(deny_reason=)` so it is recorded
  (`MCP_ASK_NO_LONGER_ALLOWED_MESSAGE`). Every door call passes
  `deadline_s=_tool_deadline(config)`. `_grant_now` repeats the tail of
  `PaneTokenStore.resolve`; a `grant_for(pane_id)` there would make it one.
  Pin: `tests/test_third_plan_g17_door_call.py`.
